title: Two Reformed affirmations — Scripture's full substance; no equal unwritten word
source_text: XXV. Duo igitur affirmamus. Et primo quidem omnia quae pertinent ad substantiam fidei & religionis plene & sufficienter in Scriptura sacra contineri. Deinde, praeter Scripturam non extare ullum Dei verbum quod fidei nostrae sit principium & regula, adeoque nullas traditiones non scriptas aequalis esse cum sacra Scriptura authoritatis. Minime vero istud honoris tribuendum esse traditionibus illis quas Ecclesia Romana tanquam Apostolicas & divinas commendat. Prius autem illud sequitur ex posteriori. Etenim si nullum sit praeter Scripturam Dei verbum, necesse est illam omnia ad fidem & salutem necessaria continere, vel nos jam aliquibus necessariis carere. Et quod inde sequitur, nullam certam ad salutem nobis superesse viam. Itaque omissis iis testimoniis quibus Scriptura suam ipsius plenitudinem & perfectionem commendat, illud praecipue probare contendemus nullum esse Dei verbum viva voce tantum traditum quod cum Scriptura sacra certa sit fidei regula.
pass_a_gloss: We therefore affirm two things. And first, that all things pertaining to the substance of faith and religion are fully and sufficiently contained in sacred Scripture. Then, that besides Scripture there exists no word of God that is a principle and rule of our faith, and so that no unwritten traditions are of equal authority with sacred Scripture. Least of all is that honor to be given to those traditions which the Roman Church recommends as Apostolic and divine. But the former follows from the latter. For if there is no word of God besides Scripture, it is necessary that Scripture contain all things necessary to faith and salvation, or else that we already lack some necessary things. And what follows from that: that no certain way of salvation remains for us. Therefore, setting aside those testimonies by which Scripture recommends its own fullness and perfection, we will chiefly contend to prove that there is no word of God handed down by living voice alone that is a certain rule of faith together with sacred Scripture.
pass_b_english: First: everything belonging to the substance of faith and religion is fully and sufficiently in sacred Scripture.

Second: besides Scripture there is no word of God that is our faith's principle and rule — so no unwritten traditions equal Scripture's authority, and least of all Rome's so-called Apostolic and divine traditions.

The first follows from the second: if there is no divine word outside Scripture, Scripture must hold all that faith and salvation require, or we already lack necessities and have no sure path of salvation.
So, without rehearsing Scripture's own fullness-texts, the main proof target is this: no living-voice-only word of God stands as a certain faith-rule alongside Scripture.
